newsitem.title: CZECH REPUBLIC: CZECH C.BANK PROPOSES CSOB, SPORITELNA MERGER - PAPER.
newsitem.headline: CZECH C.BANK PROPOSES CSOB, SPORITELNA MERGER - PAPER.

text.p: The Czech National Bank (CNB) has called for the fast privatisation of the state stakes in bank IPB a.s. and for merger of savings bank Ceska Sporitelna a.s. and Ceskoslovenska Obchodni Banka a.s., an economic daily reported on Wednesday.

The daily Hospodarske Noviny said that the central bank had alreday submitted the plan to the cabinet whose final approval is necessary for such a move. The basic contents of the story were confirmed to Reuters by a senior central bank official.

The paper quoted central bank sources as saying that the proposed merger would create the largest bank in the region, but it would be necessary to delay its full privatisation for three to five years until effects of the merger are analysed.
The proposal does not plan a fast selloff of the largest Czech commercial bank, Komercni Banka a.s. , it said.
The senior central bank official told Reuters that the plan was written from the point of view of the central bank as a regulator, and whether the cabinet will agree is still unclear.

The official said however that there was broad agreement on the need to go forward with the privatisation of remaining state stakes in the so-called "Big Four" banks which control more than 70 percent of the country's banking activity.

Ceska Sporitelna, in which the state still holds a 45 percent stake after the government's stock vouchers for citizens programme, is the largest state savings bank where most Czechs put their money during the communist era.
It still holds a majority of Czech retail deposits.

CSOB, born as a foreign trade bank in the former communist state banking system, is owned by a variety of Czech and Slovak state institutions including both the central banks and the Czech National Property Fund, with small stakes privately held.
Hospodarske Noviny quoted CNB governor Josef Tosovsky as saying large Czech banks need strong starategic partners which can cover the share purchase frorm their own resources.
Such investors do not exist domestically, and the CNB wants to find them abroad through tenders, it reported him as saying.
He said privatisaiton was needed because the state is passive in the banks and private investors would push for higher efficiency, making the banks more competitive abroad.

Finance Minister Ivan Kocarnik said earlier this month that he also wanted the state's stake in IPB to be the first to be privatised, and that a strageic foreign partner taking the stake would be the most likely option.
Nomura International and Dutch ING NV have been widely seen as potential partners for the bank, although top officials of both banks have declined comment on their possible interest in IPB.
It is not clear when the cabinet will debate the CNB proposals, but the senior central bank official said it might be on the agenda of next Wednesday's government meeting.
